clue.text: Graham's pa upset Dickensian brolly woman

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's father has been upset by a brolly-wielding woman out of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges GRAHAMSPA (the possessive's S counts here). Sarah Gamp is the nurse in Martin Chuzzlewit whose umbrella gave British English 'gamp' for a brolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Gamp is the umbrella-carrying nurse in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Performances from the New Testament

definitions.meaning: performances on stage, turns or routines
a book taken from the New Testament, after the Gospels

explanation.definitionFit: Stage turns are called by this name, and it is also the title of the fifth book of the Christian scriptures' second part.

clue.text: Raven disturbed above us at the classical entrance to Hell

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece above another is written before it
disturbed means stirred up, so the bird's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A raven hovers over us at the gateway to the classical underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns RAVEN into AVERN; 'above' in this down clue puts it before US.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Avernus near Naples was believed by Romans to be the way down to the underworld.

clue.text: The engineer's pivot in the fishpond

definitions.meaning: a metal pin or socket on which a hinge or shaft turns
a small freshwater fish found in ponds

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a mechanical pin on which a rudder or shaft swings and a small carp-family fish.

clue.text: Obligatory order for unfermented, grape-juice

definitions.meaning: something required, an essential
freshly pressed juice before it becomes wine

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a necessity (something obligatory) and the winemaker's term for pressed juice not yet fermented.

clue.text: Revolutionary equestrian headwear for a pantomime heroine .

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist
equestrian activity is horse riding
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A rebel's riding hat is costume for the leading lady of a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show built on fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl with the scarlet cape who meets the wolf is a stock heroine of British pantomime.

clue.text: … creates a striking report as worn by the timpanist

definitions.text: … creates a striking report as worn by the timpanist

parts.words: … creates a striking report as worn by the timpanist
parts.note: a small detonator that bangs when struck, read as a hat a drummer might wear

explanation.surface: Something makes a loud noise, as a kettledrum player's headgear might.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the panto clue before it. The first reading is the small explosive cap struck by a gun's hammer; the second treats it as a cap worn by a member of the drum section.
explanation.definitionFit: A small charge fired by a blow, once used to ignite guns and toy pistols, makes a sharp bang.

clue.text: Could it best be used for cleaning down?

definitions.text: Could it best be used for cleaning down?

parts.words: Could it best be used for cleaning down?
parts.note: 'down' is the soft plumage of birds, and a cleaning tool made of plumes seems fitted for it

explanation.surface: A question about the best tool for cleaning downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction; it is soft feathers, the stuff this household tool is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A household tool of plumes on a stick used to whisk dust from surfaces.

clue.text: Wooden-headed source of intellect in Essex

indicators.note: headed means led by, so the thinking organ comes in front of the timber piece

parts.note: the brain is where thought comes from
wooden things come from a tree, the source of wood

explanation.surface: A blockheaded thinker from the home counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden-headed' looks like one insult, but 'headed' says the wooden part, TREE, is topped by BRAIN. Essex is a county just east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Braintree is a market town in the county of Essex, so the clue places it there.

clue.text: Novel race for a basic Fleet Street commodity

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: A fresh contest for something every newspaper office needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was the home of the British national press, so it stands for newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap paper that newspapers are printed on was the raw material of the press.

clue.text: Academician joins sappers. How unusual!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: An artist joins the army engineers, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' is a link putting the two abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation at something seldom seen means it is uncommon.

clue.text: Supplementary building to remove wrongfully

definitions.meaning: an extension or wing added to a main building
to seize or take territory without right

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an extra wing of a building; the verb means to seize territory unlawfully.

clue.text: In the end, moustache can be a pain in the neck

indicators.note: the end of the word moustache holds a run of letters, the tail of that word

explanation.surface: A whiskery man finds his moustache a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the closing four letters of 'moustache'; 'can be' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull throbbing pain such as a stiff neck brings is a familiar kind of soreness.

clue.text: Panamanian punctuation mark

definitions.meaning: Colón is a port city of Panama at the Caribbean end of the canal
the two-dot mark that introduces a list or explanation

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Panamanian port city (Colón) and the two-dot stop used before a list.

clue.text: Surrounded by cultivated mango

indicators.note: cultivated means worked like soil, so the fruit's letters are turned over

explanation.surface: Grown in the middle of a mango plantation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the midst of others is to be enclosed by them.

clue.text: No way out where stay-at-homes stay

definitions.text: No way out where stay-at-homes stay

parts.words: No way out where stay-at-homes stay
parts.note: people who stay at home remain inside the house rather than going out through the doors

explanation.surface: Homebodies stay put with no exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as IN DOORS: in, not out, behind the doors, which is where homebodies remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside a building, not out in the open air, is where homebodies keep themselves.

clue.text: Just retribution seems in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder means jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fair punishment appears to be in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disorder' rearranges SEEMSIN; the 'in' of 'seems in' is fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Named for the Greek goddess of retribution, it means the downfall that someone has earned.

clue.text: Wrapping that's of little use. to the swordsman

definitions.meaning: thin metal sheet used to wrap food

definitions.text: of little use. to the swordsman
definitions.meaning: a fencing sword made of tin would be flimsy and useless

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a foil is a fencing sword, and one made of tin would bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet used to wrap food; and a fencer's blade of weak metal would be worthless.

clue.text: Inside information of mean quality

definitions.meaning: the true facts, known to insiders
contemptible, base or despicable

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the true facts on something; the adjective means base and despicable.

clue.text: N. African city of broken granite construction

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the stone's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A North African city built of crushed granite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Scold in a chirpy sense

definitions.meaning: one who twits, taunting or reproaching someone
to chirp as small birds do

explanation.definitionFit: One who twits, or taunts, is a scold; birds' light rapid chirping goes by the same word.

clue.text: Sound return in the choir .

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words the choir

explanation.surface: Sound comes back in the singing choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound coming back off a wall is a returning sound.

clue.text: American writer's double

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., author of Huckleberry Finn
an old word for two, as in 'never the ... shall meet'

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain wrote Tom Sawyer, and the archaic word means a pair or two.

clue.text: Briefly nameless soon in the old way

definitions.meaning: the short form of anonymous, as written under an unsigned poem
an archaic word meaning presently or shortly

explanation.definitionFit: It abbreviates 'anonymous' and is an archaic word for presently, shortly.

clue.text: Blend containing an indefinite number for a sly miss

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to blend is to mix
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A mixture with an unknown quantity, to suit a crafty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, impudent girl is called this; 'miss' means a young woman.

clue.text: Where the writer cultivates his theme?

definitions.text: Where the writer cultivates his theme?

parts.words: Where the writer cultivates his theme?
parts.note: a patch of ground where a gardener grows things, read as an author's storyline

explanation.surface: A question about where an author works on a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivates' points at a garden patch; a novel's storyline goes by the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of growing ground and a story's sequence of events share the word.

clue.text: Where the gymnast might drink flat beer?

definitions.text: Where the gymnast might drink flat beer?

parts.words: Where the gymnast might drink flat beer?
parts.note: 'flat' read as level and a pub counter as a gymnastics apparatus

explanation.surface: A question about where an athlete would drink stale ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat beer' suggests stale ale, but read flat as level and the pub as the gym rail used for swings.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised steel rail used for swinging routines in men's gymnastics.

clue.text: Excuse former single payment to local council

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
one is single
rates were the British local property tax paid to the council

explanation.surface: A one-off payment to the council lets a former resident off.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British property tax paid to local councils before 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from blame is to clear them; 'excuse' is used here as a verb.
